title: Scenario uses {MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR} but the runner docs only define {MOVE_IN_DATE}
evidence:
+  `{MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR}` keeps the pin exactly one month past the
+  12-month bound forever — no yearly bump needed.
---
+  desired_move_in_date: "{MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR}"
---
+   - `{MOVE_IN_DATE}` → today + 90 days as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. `date -v+90d +%F`)
detail: The scenario's promise relies on a template key the SKILL.md substitution list never defines — only {MOVE_IN_DATE} is added. Unsubstituted, the literal string posts and hits the parse-failure branch, not the upper-bound branch this scenario exists to exercise.
recommended_fix: Document {MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR} (today + 13 months, YYYY-MM-DD) in the SKILL.md substitution step and template-keys section alongside {MOVE_IN_DATE}.

title: SKILL.md claims both boundary scenarios "pin literal dates on purpose" while the same diff un-pins too-far-future
evidence:
+- `{MOVE_IN_DATE}` — today + 90 days (YYYY-MM-DD, computed at fill time). **Every non-validation scenario must use this for `desired_move_in_date`** — hardcoded calendar dates go stale and the server rejects past dates (the whole suite went red on this once, 2026-08). Only the boundary-validation scenarios (`desired-move-in-date-in-past`, `-too-far-future`) pin literal dates on purpose.
---
-  desired_move_in_date: "2030-01-01"
+  desired_move_in_date: "{MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR}"
detail: The new template-keys sentence says desired-move-in-date-too-far-future pins a literal date, but the scenario hunk in this same diff replaces the literal "2030-01-01" with a template variable. The statement is stale on arrival.
recommended_fix: Reword to name only desired-move-in-date-in-past as pinning a literal date, and describe too-far-future as using the computed {MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR} key.

title: Layout-changes heading says RC1.1; every bullet and flow step says RC1.2
evidence:
+### Layout changes since 2026-08 (F1/F4 + RC1.1)
---
+- **RC1.2:** `reference_contact_choice` (`attested`/`declined`) is mandatory server-side and its attestation card closes the References section — scenarios answer it per flow step 12 (branches predating the card inject a hidden input instead).
detail: The section header attributes the attestation work to RC1.1 while the bullet beneath it, flow step 12, and the new stepper scenario all say RC1.2. Two labels for one change invites mis-citation later.

title: form_stepper.js claims the form.js marker is "set at the top of form.js" — the diff places it at line ~430
evidence:
+    // targets. Bail to the (submittable) long form instead. The marker is
+    // set at the top of form.js, so its presence proves the file executed.
---
@@ -430,6 +430,10 @@ window.__rtRecomputeSubmitDisabled = function () {
detail: The formJsRan guard's correctness rationale is that the marker is set at the top of form.js, proving execution. The diff's own hunk header locates `window.__rtRecomputeSubmitDisabled = function () {` around line 430 — mid-file, not top. Presence proves only that execution reached line ~430; a later-throwing condition-engine pass is exactly the failure the comment claims to exclude.
recommended_fix: Correct the comment to state what the marker actually proves (execution reached its definition site), or move a dedicated early-execution marker to the top of form.js.

title: listing_source_options is now production code retained solely for a parity test that can no longer detect drift
evidence:
+/// Whitelist of listing-source values accepted by the handler. The form no
+/// longer asks the question (F4 field diet, 2026-08: the self-reported
+/// acquisition signal wasn't scoring-relevant and cost a control on the
+/// longest step) — this const remains as the form-side mirror of
+/// `application_handler.is_valid_listing_source` for the parity test, so a
+/// stale cached page can still post the field without a validation error.
---
-      form_fields.view_select_field(
-        name: "listing_source",
detail: The select is deleted, so nothing renders these options; the parity test now compares the handler whitelist against a const only the test reads — it cannot catch form/handler drift because there is no form side left. The trailing 'so a stale cached page...' clause also misattributes posting tolerance to the const rather than the handler.
recommended_fix: Either move the accepted-values list next to the handler (where it does work) and test that, or drop the const and test is_valid_listing_source directly against the DB-constraint whitelist.

title: two_pass step re-navigates to $NAV_URL unconditionally, ignoring the stepper:true STEP_NAV_URL rule
evidence:
+2. **Navigate** to `$NAV_URL` (= `$FORM_URL` plus `rt_consent_test=1` and `stepper=off`). The query-string flags tell consent.js to auto-accept essential-only so the cookie banner doesn't intercept clicks, and disable the F1 stepper so the whole long form is fillable. **If the scenario sets `stepper: true`, navigate to `$STEP_NAV_URL` instead** (no `stepper=off`) and drive the stepper per the scenario-keys section. (No login — public form.)
---
+18. **If `two_pass: true`**: re-navigate to `$NAV_URL`, repeat fill+submit, then verify the pass-2 outcome against `expected_outcome`. Pass-1 must always be `confirmation` for two-pass scenarios.
detail: Step 2 carves out stepper:true scenarios to use STEP_NAV_URL, but the pass-2 re-navigation in step 18 names $NAV_URL without the carve-out. Any future two-pass stepper scenario would silently lose the stepper on its second pass.
recommended_fix: Amend step 18 to re-navigate to the same URL the scenario used for pass 1 (STEP_NAV_URL when stepper: true, else NAV_URL).
